text:
Alex (Sales): Hey team -- ACME asked for our SOC2/ISO artifacts + the pen-test signatory. Quick q: do we need the pen-test letter to be signed by the third-party vendor directly, or is a Redwood-attested summary okay for the POC? They want to include it in their procurement dataroom by EOD Friday.
Maria (Security): For procurement + legal, they usually want the vendor-signed attestation. The pen-test letter should come from the external testing firm (signed PDF). We can supplement with a Redwood cover letter that explains scope and environment.
Devon (SRE): FYI for the pen-test scope: if the test hits staging, we'll need to provision the ephemeral IPs and a dedicated creds sandbox. @Alex please confirm which env they want.
Sam (Engineering): Also flag on pricing: if they request Dedicated or single-tenant for the POC (to satisfy control requirements), that could change the cost estimate. We should surface the delta now.
Alex (Sales): Good point. ACME originally asked for shared-hosted POC but legal pushed back on shared tenancy. I'll ask them to confirm if they need Dedicated for the POC.
Maria (Security): Actionable artifact list for the dataroom (what we can provide this week): 1) SOC2 Type II summary + cover (PDF) 2) ISO27001 scope statement excerpt (PDF) 3) Signed pen-test letter from vendor OR signed attestation from vendor + Redwood cover note 4) Network diagram + staging IP whitelist (SVG/PDF) 5) KMS/crypto control high-level description (doc)
Alex (Sales): Nice, can you drop the exact filenames we should upload to the dataroom? Also timeline — can we get the vendor-signed pen-test letter by Friday if we request it today?
Maria (Security): Filenames: `SOC2_Redwood_summary_2025.pdf`, `ISO27001_scope_excerpt_2024.pdf`, `pen_test_letter_VENDOR_signed.pdf` (or `pen_test_vendor_attestation_plus_redwood_cover.pdf`), `staging_network_diagram.pdf`, `kms_control_summary.pdf`.
Maria (Security): About timeline: depends on the vendor. If the test was already done and they have a report, we can request a signed letter today and many vendors can return a simple signed attestation within 48-72 hours. If they need a new test scheduled, that's weeks. Ask ACME whether they already have a vendor report or just need an attestation.
ComplianceBot: :white_check_mark: New internal ticket created: COMP-4821 for "ACME dataroom artifacts & pen-test signatory" assigned to Maria. ETA fields updated: vendor-letter request (48-72h), dataroom upload (after receipt). Link: https://tickets.internal/COMP-4821
Alex (Sales): I'll ping ACME to clarify vendor status and tenancy requirement. If they need Dedicated POC, Sam — can you rough the monthly delta? Even a ballpark helps.
Sam (Engineering): Ballpark: Dedicated single-tenant POC (1x A100 equiv) + managed infra + support uplift ~ $18k-28k/mo depending on burst capacity. I'll refine if they give expected qps and seq lengths.
Alex (Sales): Perfect. One more: Devon, can you paste the minimal command/snippet we give to vendors for staging access (ephemeral creds flow)?
Devon (SRE): Sure — send them this (we'll rotate creds on acceptance):
```
# request ephemeral creds
curl -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.ai/ephemeral-creds \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <vendor_api_key>" \
  -d '{"scope":"staging-read","duration":3600}'
```
Devon (SRE): We'll expect vendors to run tests from those IP ranges only; I'll attach the IP CIDR list in a follow-up.
Alex (Sales): Great — I'll update ACME and reply here. Thanks everyone :pray:
